dialogues.speaker: Zotov
dialogues.text: This job really is tough, having to worry every single day... Oh no, what if the commander holds this against me? I only just got here...

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Tch. One slap and you're already panicking? You haven't seen anything yet. Take it from someone who knows, kid. Go home and build some muscle.

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Look at you, a stiff breeze could knock you flat. Give it a few days. Once the Veche holds a real meeting, you'll understand exactly what I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Zotov
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait... Why would a council meeting have anything to do with us?

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: What do you think we're there for? If they're in that room for hours, we're standing outside for hours! And after a while, you'll be thirsty, dead tired, and stuck listening to the councilors drone on about whatever boring nonsense they feel like arguing over.

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Then your head starts to dip for one second, and suddenly they're saying you "disrespected the councilors." At that point, getting slapped or losing your job would be getting off easy.

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Back when I was your age, I did seven straight days on guard duty! Seven! Look at you. You really think you could make it through that?

dialogues.speaker: Zotov
dialogues.text: Oh! So that's what you meant! That's why you told me to go home and train!

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Hmph. Now you're catching on. When I was new, nobody bothered to explain this stuff to me. You should be grateful, kid.

dialogues.speaker: Zotov
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... Slavina, didn't you just nod off while you were standing guard?

dialogues.speaker: Slavina
dialogues.text: Y-You don't get it! I was sleeping on my feet with my eyes open! That's a veteran skill. Take notes!
